why: The statement names 'numerous conjectures', so every settled sub-case (the regular odd two-dimensional case over Q at a given prime, the irregular residually reducible case, the totally real ordinary weight-{0,1} cases, the even case, and the unramified cases) is a case, never the whole. Chojecki's conditional pro-modular result and Feuerpfeil's tame pro-p statement concern changed questions, so they are variants. Luo 2026, the talks and Zhang's Eisenstein v1/v2 only reformulate the conjecture or use it as an input, so they are none. Ahlqvist–Carlson does not address the conjecture. The close call is Zhang p=3. Spotting the error is criticism and earns no credit. But the acknowledgement also credits the model with 'helping him to modify the strategy of the proof in Section 5', the section the completion turns on. A strategy that the human then carried out is mathematics supplied, so I answered assisted rather than none. The OpenAI family is AI-generated by the repository's own account. Its FM2 result is the p=2 odd regular case, which is a case; it is doubtful but kept.
doubts: The Zhang p=3 credit is thin: the record cannot say how much of the new Section 5 strategy came from the model, and the attribution belongs to v5 (2026), not to the 2024 v1 date the event carries. Paškūnas's journal publication rests only on a snippet, so it is left unreviewed. The OpenAI p=2 result and Zhang's p=3 result together with Pan would cover the regular odd two-dimensional case over Q for every prime, but each piece is a separate case and none of them has been checked.
